datasets.variant_notes: Includes a separate Sanskrit-English code-mixed variant (971 questions) in addition to the 11 monolingual language sets.
datasets.annotation_method: Human annotators corrected OCR-extracted text from official UGC-NET examination PDFs (2012-2018). Native speakers with graduate-level expertise manually corrected recognition errors, restored missing characters and diacritics, normalized punctuation and spacing, and classified each question by category (language understanding vs. general knowledge) and question type. A two-step review pipeline was used: annotators corrected and aligned answers, then a senior reviewer verified against original exam papers.

data_creator_info.creator_affiliation: Indian Institute of Management Indore; BharatGen
data_creator_info.evidence: Annotation was carried out by native speakers having expertise in the target language and having prior experience reading graduate-level exam material. Annotators were compensated at a rate of $1 per 10 questions.

datasets.source_reference: UGC-NET examination papers (2012-2018) from the National Testing Agency, Government of India (https://ugcnet.nta.ac.in)
datasets.notes: Questions sourced from UGC-NET, a nationwide graduate-level examination for PhD admission and university teaching eligibility. 13,207 total questions. Post-verification audit on a random 5% sample reported WER of 0.68% and CER of 0.12%. The original questions are human-authored by government examination authorities, not by the benchmark creators.
